summary.name: Taming Operational Load with VMware CRE
summary.one_liner: A VMware Customer Reliability Engineering team's blog post describing how they measured and reduced their operational load (toil) from about 65% to 35% of their time.
use_cases: Measuring how much of an SRE team's time goes to operational work
Setting up an interrupts rotation to shield engineers from interruptions
Running a quarterly team time-investment survey
Deciding which work fits an SRE team's charter
summary.what_it_does: The post explains how VMware's CRE team defined operational load (unplanned, manual tasks that resolve a problem but do not prevent future ones) and why it scales poorly for SRE teams. It describes splitting all team time into two categories, operational and project, and assessing the split with an anonymous survey. The team's action plan included aligning work with a stakeholder-approved charter, defragmenting meetings, and creating an interrupts rotation with one interruptible engineer per week, later formalized into primary and secondary schedules. It also includes a summarized sample time-investment survey.
notable: Defines operational load with a practical litmus test and a 50% ceiling target
Describes an interrupts rotation with primary and secondary interruptible engineers
Includes a sample time-investment survey template
caveats: Describes one team's experience; the categories are intentionally broad and may not fit other teams
Closing paragraph promotes VMware Tanzu SRE workshops and sales contact
